of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChest pain since 3 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAbdominal distension since 3 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAbdominal pain since 3 days and decreased urine output since 3days and not passed stools since 3days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/sreejaboga.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss-our.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Anatomical locations and etiological possibilities:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA.Pancreas:acute severe pancreatitis secondary to gall stones\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB.Kidney:Acute kidney injury secondary to pancreatitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC.lungs:Right pleural effusion secondary to acute severe pancreatitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPleuropulmonary abnormalities are commonly associated with pancreatitis, respiratory dysfunction is rarely seen at the time of presentation to Emergency department (ED) but usually develops after fluid resuscitation. It manifests as acute lung injury or acute respiratory distress syndrome. It is one of the major components of multiple organ system dysfunction syndromes. Other manifestations are bilateral infiltrates, pleural effusion, pulmonary hypertension, and decreased thoracic compliance\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/intensive-care\/severe-acute-pancreatitis-and-its-management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ED.Tibia:diaphyseal dysplasia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EE.Right upper limb:atherosclerotic vascular disease\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Edue to hypertriglyceridemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDuring the first 1-2 wk, a pro-inflammatory response occurs, which results in systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), a sterile response in which sepsis or infection rarely occurs. If the SIRS is severe, then proinflammatory mediators can cause early multiple (respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic) organ failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4194569\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESequence of events\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA.diaphyseal dysplasia of both tibia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB.patient is a alcoholic and smoker since 30years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC.patient has an atherosclerotic vascular disease of right upper limb\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ED.patient presented with chest pain,sob, decreased urine output(due to AKI secondary to sepsis),constipation(due to paralytic ileus),abdominal distension\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe was diagnosed with acute severe pancreatitis(supported by clinical,USG findings and raised serum amylase levels) secondary to gall stones with AKI ,rt pleural effusion\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EE.patient was started on inj.lasix and iv antibiotics,after 1day pedal edema and sob decreased.after one moreday patient was in altered sensorium,on the same day patient was taken for hemodialysis 1st session.after hemodialysis his urea and creat values have come down(7.4 to 5.3)and sensorium improved.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;F.After 2days patient was taken for one more session of dialysis (his creat 5.9 to 4.4) but his total leukocyte counts have been raised ?Central line sepsis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EG.within 24hrs of 2nd session of dialysis his creat increased again to 5.4 and patient had 8episodes of vomitings and was intolerant to oral feeds.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGICAL interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.NBM:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Ryles tube:If nutritional support is supplemented by the enteral route, then it is usually delivered by tube feeding. There is a controversy about nasogastric versus nasojejunal feeding. But there is not much evidence to support any one over the other. Though traditionally nasojejunal feedings (to be delivered distal to the ligament of Treitz) have been preferred with the concept of less stimulation of the exocrine pancreas, cholecystokinin (CCK) cells that are present in the distal third part of the duodenum get stimulated when food passing through duodenum. It releases CCK that stimulates the pancreas and increased volume of pancreatic enzymes and bicarbonate secretion. This may worsen the course of the disease. Nasogastric tube feedings have now been shown to as safe as the jejunal feeding. Nasogastric insertion can be at bedside. Fluoroscopy endoscopic (endoscopically placed guide wire) and specialist help is not needed. With the Nasogastric (NG) feeding, the standard precautions of aspiration like elevation of head end of bed should be followed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/intensive-care\/severe-acute-pancreatitis-and-its-management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3:Oxygen support:Patients with acute severe pancreatitis should be monitored closely for early detection of failure. Respiratory support usually initiated by supplemental oxygen and mechanical ventilation is often required depending on the severity of respiratory dysfunction. Nasogastric decompression will decrease the distension and improve the compliance and prevent aspiration. Non-invasive ventilation is poorly tolerated in most of the patients because of abdominal distension and reduced functional residual capacity, careful selection of patient is warranted. Non-invasive ventilation is good choice to start with as it may avoid endotracheal intubation. Acute lung injury and Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to acute severe pancreatitis is similar to any other condition using lung protective strategies. Pleural effusion may need ultrasound-guided drainage. Good analgesia will help in chest physiotherapy, early physiotherapy will prevent atelectasis and related complications\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPHARMACOLOGICAL interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Iv fluids:Hypotension is one of the most common presentations with acute pancreatitis. It is a sign of impending organ dysfunction. The hypotension is due to the third space loss secondary to the inflammatory response, this contributes to hypoperfusion and end organ perfusion dysfunction. Aggressive fluid resuscitation and rapid restoration of intravascular volume are the main stay of the treatment. It requires several liters of fluids. Both crystalloids and colloids can be used as resuscitation fluids\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/intensive-care\/severe-acute-pancreatitis-and-its-management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.Diuretics:for decreased urine output and renal failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.Antibiotics:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERole of antibiotic prophylaxis in severe acute pancreatitis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProphylactic antibiotics in severe acute pancreatitis have been a topic of debate in the last 4–5 decades. Pancreatic necrosis more than 30% increases the chances of infection. The right choice of antibiotics is very important, those which have high penetration into pancreatic tissue. Carbapenems are both broad spectrum and excellent pancreatic penetration properties. Other antibiotics, which penetrate well in the pancreatic tissue, are cephalosporin, ureidopenicillins, fluoroquinolones, metronidazole and imipenem. Aminoglycosides have a poor penetration ability. Patients with mild pancreatitis do not benefit from antibiotics. In a meta-analysis by Sharma et al. [16], use of prophylactic antibiotics has shown mortality benefit in patients with Acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP) confirmed by contrast-enhanced CT (21–12.3%). Ref. [15, 16] prophylactic antibiotics use has not shown to decrease the need for interventional and surgical management but no effect on mortality.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/intensive-care\/severe-acute-pancreatitis-and-its-management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.ANALGESIA:Pain is one of the symptoms of acute severe pancreatitis. It causes discomfort and heightened sympathetic activity, impairment of oxygenation due to restriction of abdominal wall movement. Effective analgesia can be provided by the use of opioids and parenteral route, i.e. intravenous route is the preferred route. Analgesia may improve pulmonary dysfunction. In the past, morphine was supposed to exacerbate acute pancreatitis by promoting contraction of the sphincter of Oddi and increase pressure in the sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, but there is no good supportive evidence. Another modality of pain management is use of drugs like local anaesthetics through in epidural route\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/intensive-care\/severe-acute-pancreatitis-and-its-management\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECASE : 2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) A 55 year old male, shepherd by occupation, presented to the OPD with the chief complaints of fever (on and off), loss of appetite, headache, body pains, generalized weakness since 2 months, cough since 2 weeks and vomitings and pain abdomen since 2 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA) Where are the different anatomical locations of the patient's problems and what are the different etiologic possibilities for them? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EANATOMICAL LOCATIONS WITH ETIOLOGY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBONE MARROW\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiology: Multiple myeloma\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKIDNEYS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiology: AKI due to multiple myeloma\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHEMATOLOGICAL (ANEMIA)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiology: secondary to multiple myeloma\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELUNGS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiology: Tuberculosis (Increased susceptibility to infections)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETIMELINE OF EVENTS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol \u0026amp; smoking (35 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStopped alcohol (4 years)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFever , generalised weakness \u0026amp; anemia - 2 units blood transfusion (1.5 years)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStopped smoking (4 months)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELow grade fever , generalized weakness , headache , neck pain , loss of appetite , weight loss (2 months)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECough \u0026amp; SOB (2 weeks)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVomiting \u0026amp; pain abdomen (2 days)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOUTCOME:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESome symptomatic relief and referred to higher centre in need for oncologist\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB) What are the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the management of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of them?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPHARMACOLOGIC :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.ANTIBIOTICS : For underlying infection (Azithromycin for ?Atypical pneumonia)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.ATT : For TB\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.SEVELAMER : For hyperphosphatemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.FEBUXOSTAT : For hyperuricemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.PRBC transfusion for anemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECase 3:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttp:\/\/nithishaavula.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/51-yr-old-male-with-hfref.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)pedal edema with abdominal distention with sob suggestive of right heart failure or renal failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB)etilogy of rt heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK459381\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Echronic conditions of pressure overload may lead to RVF. These include:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrimary pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and secondary pulmonary hypertension (PH) as seen in chronic-obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or pulmonary fibrosis)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECongenital heart disease (pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, or a systemic RV).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe following conditions result in volume overload causing RVF:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EValvular insufficiency (tricuspid or pulmonic)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECongenital heart disease with a shunt (atrial septal defect (ASD) or anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR)).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnother important mechanism that leads to RVF is intrinsic RV myocardial disease. This includes:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERV ischemia or infarct\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInfiltrative diseases such as amyloidosis or sarcoidosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EArrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECardiomyopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMicrovascular disease.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELastly, RVF may be caused by impaired filling which is seen in the following conditions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConstrictive pericarditis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETricuspid stenosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESystemic vasodilatory shock\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECardiac tamponade\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESuperior vena cava syndrome\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHypovolemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr khaini (3 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPins and needles (1 year)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPalpitations (8 months)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPND (3 months)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E!\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPedal edema and SOB (2 months)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECURRENT OUTCOME:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECompletly relieved of his symptoms as the wet beriberi resolved.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB) What are the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the management of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of them?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPHARMACOLOGIC :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.LASIX : Mortality: 3 placebo-controlled trials (n=221) reported data; the OR was 0.25 (95% confidence interval, CI: 0.07, 0.84, P=0.03), representing an absolute risk reduction of 8% in mortality in patients treated with diuretics compared to placebo.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWorsening of heart failure: 4 placebo-controlled trials (n=448) and 4 active-controlled trials (n=177) reported data. The OR was 0.31 (95% CI: 0.15, 0.62, P=0.001) for the placebo-controlled trials and 0.34 (95% CI:0.10, 1.21, P=0.10) for the active-controlled trials.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.THIAMINE : In the study by Schoenenberger and colleagues (n=9), patients who took thiamine had 3.30% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.63%, 5.97%) greater LVEF compared to those on placebo.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELikewise, Shimon et al reported that thiamine resulted in 2.20% greater LVEF than the placebo group (n=29), although the extra improvement was not significant (95% CI: −18.97, 23.37%).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn our meta analysis, thiamine supplementation resulted in a significantly improved net change in LVEF (3.28%, 95% CI: 0.64%, 5.93%) compared with placebo.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3865826\/#:~:text=Compared%20with%20placebo%20(2%20trials,0.64%25%2C%205.93%25).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.TELMISARTAN : For afterload reduction in heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGIC :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.SALT AND FLUID RESTRICTION :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23787719\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIndividualized salt and fluid restriction can improve signs and symptoms of CHF with no negative effects on thirst, appetite, or QoL in patients with moderate to severe CHF and previous signs of fluid retention\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/nikithareddy59.blogspot.com\/feeds\/2571372900774815721\/comments\/default","title":"Post patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 60yr old male pt , farmer by occupation came to the op with\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec\/o intermittent cough with sputum since 6months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec\/o Abdominal distension since 20days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec\/o bilateral swelling asymptomatic 6months ago, then he developed cough with sputum, intermittent in nature ,sputum small in quantity, non foul smelling , non blood tinged, associated with wheeze at night time.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec\/o abdominal distension since 20days which aggravated on eating food, associated with indigestion.No loss of appetite.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ec\/o bilateral , burning micturition , guiddiness ,hematuria or decreased urine output\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShortness of breath since 15days aggravated on lying down and walking , relieved on sitting .SOB is not associated with palpitations.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPast history :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESimilar complaints of shortness of breath pedal edema and peri orbital edema 40years back for which he was admitted in Gandhi hospital where catheter was introduced through femoral artery and he was advised by the doctors to go to USA for cardiac surgery as told by the patient(records not available)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt is on inhalational bronchodilators in v\/o ??bronchial asthma (pt c\/o wheeze during night times since 6months)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o occupational internal assessment"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003ECase 1:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQ1 What is the\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Reason for this patients ascites ?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; The most common cause of Ascites is\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003ECirrhosis of liver\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; risk factors in this patient :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;1. Chronic alcoholism since 40 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;2. Truncal obesity leading to metabolic syndrome causing NAFLD leading to cirrhosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC6092576\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAltered echo texture of liver due to Cirrhosis causes portal hypertension leading to increased hydrostatic pressure causing fluid accumulation hence Ascites\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQ2\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;Bilateral pedal oedema which is of pitting type is due to decrease in the albumin level trends due to course of the disease and long standing cirrhosis causing decrease in the production of proteins causing decrease in the oncotic pressure leading to accumulation of fluid.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eas per the given clinical data due to chronic liver disease there was increasing trend of INR which was as high as 4.7 causing bleeding manifestations ( bleeding gums, hematoma formation )\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eulcerations are due his limited self practising manoeuvres done in inappropriate conditions such as\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eimproper dressing of the wound, not maintaining aseptic conditions , indescriminate use of steroids (self medication) to quote from history (\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EPatient attenders were giving history of multiple self medications whenever patient developed fever or shortness of breath they used to take decadron injections, larigo tablets,monocef and pantop over 4 months intermittently\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"Roboto, sans-serif\" style=\"background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;)\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;causing ? immune suppression leading to secondary infections hence cellulitis and non healing of wound.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQ3\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003EReason for Asterexis and constructional apraxia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003EAsterixis is a clinical sign that describes the inability to maintain sustained posture with subsequent brief, shock-like, involuntary movements.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px; margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003Ethis clinical sign is not pathognomonic for any condition. However, it may indicate a serious underlying disease process.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK535445\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWest haven criteria is being used for HE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003EIn hepatic encephalopathy (due to\u0026nbsp;cirrhosis of liver ) damage occurs to brain cells due to the impaired metabolism of ammonia is predominantly related\u0026nbsp;to the development of asterixis in hepatic encephalopathy,\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003Epathophysiology of HE\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E1 role of neurotoxins,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E2.impaired neurotransmission due to metabolic changes in liver failure, changes in brain energy metabolism, systemic inflammatory response and alterations of the blood brain barrier which produces a wide spectrum of nonspecific neurological and psychiatric manifestations.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5421503\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003Elactulose and rifaximin\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003Eunderlying mechanism of Giving lactulose\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003EThe human small intestinal mucosa does not have the enzymes to split lactulose, and hence lactulose reaches the large bowel unchanged.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003Ebasically three\u0026nbsp;mechanisms have been described on usage of lactulose\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E1.First, the colonic metabolism of sugars causes a laxative effect via an increase in intraluminal gas formation and osmolality which leads to a reduction in transit time and intraluminal pH. This laxative effect is also beneficial for constipation.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E2. lactulose promotes increased uptake of ammonia by colonic bacteria which utilize the trapped colonic ammonia as a nitrogen source for protein synthesis. The reduction of intestinal pH facilitates this process, which favors the conversion of ammonia (NH3) produced by the gut bacteria, to ammonium (NH4+),\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;an ionized form of the molecule, unable to cross biological membranes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E3. lactulose also causes a reduction in intestinal production of ammonia. The acidic pH destroys urease-producing bacteria involved in the production of ammonia. \u0026nbsp;The unabsorbed disaccharide also inhibits intestinal glutaminase activity, which blocks the intestinal uptake of glutamine, and its metabolism to ammonia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003Ehigh protein diet (2eggs \/ day) for decreased albumin synthesis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E1. Air or water bed\u0026nbsp;to prevent pressure bed sores in the dependent areas\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E2.
